passage:
Dilnaz had kept the school's mid-day meal register in Kharsi village for three years. She knew how many sacks of dal came in each month and how many plates went out.
Since spring, four sacks a month weren't adding up. And she had seen, twice, Rafiq's cousin's tempo outside the storeroom at dawn.
Rafiq was the storekeeper. He had helped her get this job when no one else would. He had come to her wedding. His wife sent her pickle every winter.
She watched the children queue with their steel plates. The dal was almost water now.
If she spoke, Rafiq could lose everything. She could lose her job; the headmistress was his relative. People would call her ungrateful.
If she said nothing, the thin dal would continue.
That night she couldn't eat. At dawn she took the register, her notes on the missing sacks, and got on the bus to the block office, her hands shaking the whole way.

qa.q: How many sacks a month were not adding up?
qa.a: Four sacks a month were not adding up.

qa.q: What feelings were pulling at Dilnaz?
qa.a: Dilnaz felt loyalty and gratitude to Rafiq, fear for her job and of being called ungrateful, and a duty to the children eating thin dal.

qa.q: Which detail seems to tip Dilnaz towards speaking?
qa.a: Watching the children queue with their plates while the dal was almost water made the harm real, and taking her register and notes to the block office was a factual, proper route.

qa.q: How might Rafiq's family be affected if Dilnaz reports what she saw?
qa.a: Rafiq's family, including his wife who sends pickle every winter, could face shame and hardship, which is part of what makes the decision so painful.

grounding: A school clerk who sees food meant for children being diverted weighs loyalty to Rafiq, who helped her against the harm, and decides to speak despite the risk.

passage:
The test reports for the parking-garage floor in Rotterdam were signed "passed". Yosef, three months into his first site-engineer job, knew the samples for level two had never gone to the lab. He had seen them cracked and forgotten in the rain.
Sami, the site lead, had hired him from forty applicants and once driven him home when his car broke down. "We're behind schedule," Sami had said. "The concrete is fine. Trust me."
Yosef lay awake. Maybe it was fine. He wasn't an expert yet. But hundreds of cars would park on that floor, and people would walk under it.
If he reported it, Sami might lose his job. Yosef might lose his, or never work in this city again.
On Sunday he wrote down dates, sample numbers, the photo of the cracked cylinders. On Monday morning he opened the company's safety reporting page and sat with the cursor on "submit" for a long time.

qa.q: What did Yosef see happen to the level-two samples?
qa.a: Yosef saw them cracked and forgotten in the rain.

qa.q: What mix of feelings kept Yosef awake?
qa.a: Yosef felt loyalty to Sami, doubt about his own expertise, fear of losing his job, and a sense of duty to the people who would use the garage.

qa.q: What careful steps did Yosef take before deciding?
qa.a: He wrote down dates, sample numbers and the photo of cracked cylinders, and turned to the company's official safety reporting page.

qa.q: How might Sami see Yosef if he submits the report?
qa.a: Sami might feel betrayed after hiring him and driving him home, even though Yosef is trying to protect the people who will use the garage.

grounding: A young engineer who sees safety tests faked weighs loyalty to the lead who hired him and fear for his job against harm to others, and prepares to speak.

passage:
I'm Bidisha, and two years ago I was a site engineer on a school building in Siliguri. One Tuesday I saw the lab report for the columns. The concrete was weaker than the design required. Tarun sir, who had hired me and taught me everything, said, "Sign the report. We'll strengthen it later. The client wants it on time."
For three nights I didn't sleep. Tarun sir had once paid for my mother's operation without being asked. Twelve workers' jobs depended on the company. My name would be finished in that small industry.
But I kept seeing children running down those corridors.
On the fourth morning I told Tarun sir to his face first. Then I wrote to the district engineer and the school trust, attached the lab report, and asked for an independent test before the next floor was poured. He never spoke to me again.
The pour was stopped. The columns were redone. I lost my job in March. I would still send that email.

qa.q: What did the lab report show about the columns?
qa.a: The concrete was weaker than the design required.

qa.q: What was Bidisha feeling during the three sleepless nights?
qa.a: Bidisha felt torn and afraid, loyal to Tarun sir and the workers yet haunted by the image of children in those corridors.

qa.q: Which step in Bidisha's decision protected people?
qa.a: Writing to the district engineer and the school trust with the lab report and asking for an independent test before the next pour, after telling Tarun sir first.

qa.q: How might Tarun sir have felt when Bidisha told him face to face?
qa.a: Tarun sir probably felt betrayed and angry, having hired and helped Bidisha, which is why he never spoke to Bidisha again.

grounding: Shows an engineer weighing loyalty to a mentor and co-workers against harm to children, and speaking up at real personal cost.

passage:
Mentor's note, Thursday evening
Damini asked to meet me at the café near her office, away from colleagues. She works in quality testing at a medicine factory. She told me she had seen her team leader, Charu, re-run tests on a batch until the results passed and delete the failed runs from the log. Twice.
She kept turning her cup. "Charu covered for me when my father was ill. The whole team loves her. If I report it, I'm the one everyone will hate." Then, more quietly: "But people will take these tablets."
She asked what I would do. I said I couldn't decide for her, but that the risk to patients was not hers to carry alone, and that she had the right to use the company's confidential reporting line and, if needed, the drug regulator. We looked up both together.
What I did next: I stayed while she wrote down dates and batch numbers and filed the report on the confidential line before we left the café. She asked me to call her tomorrow. I will.

qa.q: What did Charu delete from the log?
qa.a: The failed runs.

qa.q: What does Damini turning her cup suggest about her state?
qa.a: It suggests Damini felt torn and anxious, caught between loyalty to Charu and fear for the people who will take the tablets.

qa.q: How did the mentor support Damini without deciding for her?
qa.a: The mentor said the patient risk was not hers to carry alone, looked up the confidential line and the regulator with her, and stayed while she filed the report.

qa.q: How might Charu's team see Damini after the report?
qa.a: Some may feel hurt or angry, since they love Charu, which is part of the personal risk Damini weighed.

grounding: Shows an employee weighing loyalty to a kind team leader against harm to patients, with fear and duty side by side, before reporting.

passage:
Monday, 11 pm
I've written the email three times and deleted it twice.
What I know: at the ed-tech company, our sales team has been telling parents in small towns that the course "guarantees" a government job. Vasudha ma'am's script says it. Parents are taking loans. Last week a father cried on the phone when I couldn't promise him anything.
What I'm afraid of: Vasudha ma'am gave me this job when nobody else would. My team are good people with rent to pay; if this blows up, they might lose everything. And I'll be the snitch forever. Who hires a snitch?
What I can't forget: that father's voice.
Papa said, "I can't choose for you. But whatever you choose, you'll still have a home here."
At 10:48 I sent it to the company's ethics committee and the consumer helpline, with the script attached. My hands are cold. I don't feel brave. I just couldn't not.
Eshaan

qa.q: What were parents being told the course guarantees?
qa.a: A government job.

qa.q: What is Eshaan feeling after sending the email?
qa.a: Eshaan feels scared, hands cold and not at all brave, yet pushed by a duty that made staying silent impossible.

qa.q: What did Eshaan's report include, and where did it go?
qa.a: The sales script, sent to the company's ethics committee and the consumer helpline.

qa.q: How might the parents who took loans be affected by Eshaan's choice?
qa.a: They may finally get honest answers and a chance of help, instead of paying for a promise nobody could keep.

grounding: Shows an employee weighing loyalty to a boss and team against harm to parents, with doubt, fear and duty together, before reporting.

passage:
Ishita: can't sleep
Kavitha: what's up
Ishita: at the lab they signed off the water tests for the Rampur plant without running them. I saw the blank sheets
Kavitha: the drinking water plant??
Ishita: yes. my supervisor said the machine was down and the results are always fine anyway
Kavitha: that's scary
Ishita: I know. but Meena and Sunil are my people. if I report it they'll get into trouble. and I'll probably lose my job
Ishita: and we need this job at home. Papa's pension isn't enough
Kavitha: what happens if the water isn't fine
Ishita: kids drink it. whole villages
Ishita: I keep going round in circles. loyal to my team, or to people I'll never meet
Kavitha: you don't have to decide alone tonight. but whatever you decide, write down what you saw. dates, which sheets
Ishita: already started. I think I know what I'm going to do. I'm just scared
Kavitha: being scared doesn't mean you're wrong. call me before you go in tomorrow

qa.q: What did the supervisor say about the tests?
qa.a: That the machine was down and the results are always fine anyway.

qa.q: What is Ishita feeling while going round in circles?
qa.a: Ishita feels torn and scared: loyal to Meena and Sunil, worried about losing a job the family needs, yet troubled that children drink the water.

qa.q: What practical step does Kavitha suggest, and why?
qa.a: Writing down what Ishita saw, with dates and which sheets, so any report rests on facts rather than memory.

qa.q: Who else is affected by Ishita's choice, and how?
qa.a: Whole villages drinking the water could be harmed if the tests are wrong, while Meena and Sunil could face trouble if Ishita reports it.

grounding: Shows an employee who has seen skipped safety tests weighing loyalty to colleagues against harm to others and the risk to their own job.
